full_judgment: 16. On scrutiny of the evidence on record it reveals that the plaintiffs in support of their case adduced oral and documentary evidence. However, on perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that both the Courts below did not discuss the evidence of the plaintiffs in their respective judgments in its legal perspective. However, they opined that there is no cogent evidence on record to show that Surendra, Nath Sardar had any other property beside the suit land. They also opined that the certified copy of S.A. Khatian Ext.1-series show that even the homestead of Surendra Nath Sardar included in the probate case. It is not natural that Surendra Nath Sardar executed the "will" in respect of the suit property Ir. including his homestead depriving his wife and son from his property. The relationship between the plaintiffs and Surendra Nath Sardar and the relationship between the plaintiffs and executor Bharat Chandra Sardar has not been disclosed in the plaint. Surendra Nath Sardar died at Golapdaha under the P.S. Dumuria, District Khulna on 8th Chaitra, 1373 B.S. But P.W.2 Bishnupada Dhali in his examination-in-chief stated that Surendra Nath Sardar died in India. Form the above discussions of the Courts below, it appears that except one sentence of P.W.2 Bishnupada Dhali quoted in the judgment of both the Courts below others are mere imagination and after thought speculation. However, other evidence which are on record not discussed by both the Courts below. It appears from the discussions of the evidence that the plaintiffs adduced the evidence to prove their right, title and interest over the suit land but both the Courts below opined that they did not disclose the-x relationship with Surendra Nath Sardar. In this point I am of the view that it is not the case of revocation to prove the relationship of legatees and testator and genuineness of the "will". The defendants even did not deny the plaintiff case and proved the enlistment of enemy property by adducing any oral or documentary evidence. Even they did not produce any scrap of papers before the trial Court in favour of their claim showing that the suit land was declared and enlisted as enemy property in due process of law. However, the plaintiffs as petitioners by filing a supplementary affidavit before this Court submits the Annexure-E, which is the certified copy of order dated 4.11.1969 passed by District delegate Subordinate Judge, Khulna and some original deeds, i.e., Annexure-F series and they also produced the certified copy of the annexure-A original "will" with the revisional application which was obtained from the Court of District Judge, Khulna. On perusal of the said documents it appears that the "will" itself speaks about the relationship of Surendra Nath Sardar with legatees and it is the self explanatory "will" from which it is crystal clear that there is a good relationship between the legatees and Surendra Nath Sardar. So, both the Courts below without considering the recital and above legal aspects of the "will" as well as the order of probate and letter of administration passed in Miscellaneous case dismissed the suit which tainted by misreading and misconstruing the evidence on record. Had the learned Judges of the Courts below paid title more attention with their judicial mind to the above oral and documentary evidence they would have seen some thing more for which the decisions of the Courts below would have found affirmative. More-so, from the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the defendants in their written statement did not inscribe any thing on what date and on what basis they claimed the suit land as enemy property nor they submitted the sensor list or an iota of documentary evidence that the suit land is the enemy property. Even the defendants did not examined the alleged lessees nor produced any lease agreements, DCR and any supporting papers to establish that the suit properties were declared as enemy property in due course of law and possessed by the Government. From the defence case, it appears that in written statement they disclosed the number of lease case which was for the year 67-68, on the contrary they issued D.C.R for the year 1976. Although defence did not produce any of the records of lease eases and D.C.R but we astonishingly observe that both the Courts below have failed to notice this vital aspect of the case.
